The `craft.json` explains the failure — the harness stack is "Rust + egui (eframe)", so its app-screenshot check hunts for an eframe binary that this project (per the request) doesn't build. Now resolving the investigation unknowns:
Evidence ledger is empty (analysis evidence lives in the transcript and /tmp), so I'll resolve with the design decisions as resolutions:

The cloud-ride demo is finished and verified. It's a self-contained browser page — an orange-jacketed cyclist pedals across a sea of soft clouds under a bright blue sky, with a real mirror reflection in the cloud sea below, drifting clouds, and drag-to-orbit, wheel-zoom and Space-to-pause controls; everything runs offline from the files in `app/` with no install step. I found and fixed the last rendering issue this session (the reflection was being darkened twice, and the lighting was too dim, which made the rider's dark clothing look black) — the final screenshot now shows the rider's colors matching the reference almost exactly, and the automated check of that screenshot passes with no errors. The two automated project checks pass for the build; the harness's own screenshot check can't run because it's configured to expect a desktop app rather than a website, which is a settings mismatch outside the demo itself, not a flaw in the demo. The one thing I couldn't recover from the reference is the exact animation speeds (the pictures carry no timing), so I chose calm, dreamy motion that matches the described feel. A nice next step would be adding a slow automatic camera drift so the ride feels even more like a film sequence.
